note: Narrative gives approximately 30 minutes into flight. The abstract describes about 30 minutes of unpressurized exposure, which has a different origin.
Emergency presentation for persistent dyspnea and substernal chest pain, about one hour after landing.
Recompression began about three hours after seeking medical attention.
Deterioration with respiratory distress and ventricular fibrillation. About 2.5 hours from entering the treatment chamber and seven hours from first symptoms.
Witnesses noted sweating and distress as the cabin began repressurizing. The individual had in-flight breathing difficulty and transient inability to move the right arm per subsequent handoff.
The first ambulance assessment after landing found respiratory symptoms and weak distal pulses. The examiner observed movement of all limbs.
Shock and organ dysfunction progressed during emergency care. Fatal cardiac arrest occurred the next morning before the contemplated hyperbaric transfer.
The medical examiner recorded aerospace DCS as cause of death, with underlying cardiovascular and metabolic conditions as contributing factors.
